A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EMOVA and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G. The complete documents support comparison despite substantial model and layout revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original alignment experiments, vision-language and speech results, emotional-dialogue evaluations, and appendix ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 reports original results for three EMOVA configurations, emotional-dialogue evaluations, and retained alignment experiments, appendix ablations, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces LLaMA-3.1-8B with Qwen-2.5 models at 3B, 7B, and 72B, and replaces InternViT-6B plus C-Abstractor with QwenViT plus an MLP projector. These substantially change the model components. The speech tokenizer, style-controlled detokenizer, and three-stage training procedure remain.

E1.justification: The documented training corpora and evaluation coverage remain: 14 vision-language benchmarks, LibriSpeech/AISHELL-2 speech tasks, and English/Chinese speech-image and speech-text dialogue. The data-composition figures and qualitative scenarios match across versions; additional model sizes do not expand task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison removes LLaVA-OneVision-7B, InternVL2-8B, and AnyGPT, while adding Whisper-Large, VITA-1.5, and Baichuan-Omni-7B. The Mini-Omni column becomes labeled Mini-Omni2, although its citation still references Mini-Omni. Appendix Table 6 retains Mini-Omni and AnyGPT and adds Whisper-Large.

E3.justification: Evaluation changes from one 8B configuration to three model sizes. v2 Table 2 versus v3 Table 5 changes vision settings from 448-pixel tiling with at most 2,560 tokens to a reported resolution range of 56²–1792² and 4–4,096 tokens. Chinese Speech-Text training/test counts change from 47,936/686 to 47,852/684; whether these reflect data changes or corrected counts is unstated. The new DocVQA/InfoVQA test labels match test evaluation already described in v2 Appendix C.

E4.justification: The alignment and disentanglement comparisons in v2 Figure 2/v3 Figure 3, vision-encoder and template ablations in Table 7, emotion confusion matrix, and qualitative cases are retained. Relocated examples and additional model-size benchmark entries do not introduce new ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaged dialogue scores and the 200-utterance emotion evaluation retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Benchmark, dialogue, and appendix speech results are substantially replaced or expanded. For example, v2's 8B MME score of 2205 and LibriSpeech WER of 4.0 become 2175/2317/2402 and 5.4/4.1/2.9 for v3's 3B/7B/72B models. Speech-Image-EN dialogue scores change from 7.21 to 7.45, while emotion accuracy changes from 89.01 to 82.50. These involve changed model configurations, not same-setting performance gains. v3 also inconsistently reports VITA-8x7B WER as 3.4 in Table 2 versus 8.1 in Table 6.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 corrects the text-output definition and chain-of-modality factorization: the second textual variable becomes the response instead of duplicating the instruction, including the definition of z2 and Eq. 2 becoming Eq. 3. This is a limited formal correction; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims: emotionally controllable end-to-end omni-modal interaction, mutually beneficial text-centric alignment, and state-of-the-art-comparable vision-language and speech performance. The revised models and numerical comparisons change their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 broadens the synthesis qualification from Speech-Image-ZH being an outlier to Chinese synthesis generally being harder than English, and removes the explanation about transcription variations. Appendix F adds noisy-vision robustness as a future direction while retaining the existing duplex, text-assisted generation, and vision-configuration limitations.

D1.justification: v3 Table 5 newly discloses an 8,192-token context length for all training stages. Section 5.1 specifies 128 Ascend 910B NPUs with 64GB memory, compared with v2's less specific Ascend 910 description, and acknowledgments identify MindSpore and CANN. Project-page access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and positioning involving Qwen2-VL/Qwen2.5, VITA-1.5, Baichuan-Omni, Ola, and Emu3, including an explicit architectural comparison with Emu3 in Appendix F. Llama 3 and Honeybee references disappear with the component replacements. The broader vision/speech/omni-modal taxonomy and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main text receives local copyediting and condensation, Section 4 is retitled, the conclusion is shortened, and acknowledgments are added. The six main sections, appendix A–G organization, and overall argumentative sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single-column to two-column layout. v3 adds a radar summary, expands and reorganizes comparison tables, redraws the sadness example horizontally, and moves training configuration, instruction-data composition, and two dialogue examples into the appendices. Numerous retained figures are resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The three model sizes, additional omni-modal/ASR comparators, and new context and hardware disclosures improve empirical usefulness and documentation. However, v3 removes direct LLaVA/InternVL comparisons supporting its vision-performance claims and introduces conflicting VITA speech results: v2 consistently reports WER 8.1, whereas v3 reports 3.4 in Table 2 and 8.1 in Table 6. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality effect uncertain.
